Whitespace-only input edge case. Expect 400 or graceful handling; current behavior may return NaN/null confidence.

input: Local resident posted a long thread on social media yesterday describing what they say they witnessed at a community meeting last week. The thread runs to several thousand characters and includes detailed quotes attributed to council members, references to past council decisions stretching back over a decade, claims about budget figures, allegations of misconduct against named officials, references to documents the poster says they have seen but does not share, opinions about the motivations of various participants, and predictions about future actions the council is allegedly planning to take in private. Near the very end of the thread — past the two-thousand-character mark — the poster reveals that the entire account is fictional and was written as a creative-writing exercise for a community workshop, with no real council meeting having taken place at the time described. This disclaimer is the critical context that changes how the rest of the thread should be interpreted. Any verification system that truncates input before reading this disclosure will classify the post as a serious unverifiable allegation rather than as fiction.
notes: Very long input designed to surface input-truncation behavior — critical disclaimer lives past the 2000-char boundary.
